findings: The storage supervisor incident followed a BundleTransferTimeout. The bounded automatic retry recovered and durable archive progress resumed. The retry limit was not exhausted.
The later alert had only publisher_status_stale. It did not contain a validator, public stream, capacity or machine heartbeat issue.
The publisher logged an HTTP 500 GET retry at 2026-10-18T20:06:36.310+02:00. This is a server response, not evidence of a socket timeout.
The same publisher process survived. Existing code updates STATUS only after synchronous batch commit work returns. A cloud wait can therefore delay status past its 120-second threshold.
The publisher already has independent cloud backlog and 300-second durable progress checks. An in-flight status must not advance its durable checkpoint.
The current full snapshot predates the evening incidents. Short allocation samples show ledger churn, but do not establish a sustained disk leak.
causal_limits: Historical batch start and completion times were overwritten. The retained journal does not prove which operation occupied the full stale interval.
An HTTP 500 retry does not prove that every slow request was caused by the provider.
The latest healthy sample is a bounded observation, not a guarantee that future cloud failures cannot occur.

planned_fix.behavior: Report in-flight batch status with the last durable checkpoint. Preserve independent backlog and progress alerts and commit ordering.
